Pathophysiological mechanisms of long-COVID neurological manifestations and neuroprotective effects of medical gases

Pathophysiological mechanisms of long-COVID neurological manifestations and neuroprotective effects of medical gases.Schematic representation of SARS-CoV-2 neuroinvasion pathways and the neuroprotective mechanisms of medical gases in long-COVID brain fog. (A) Pathophysiology: SARS-CoV-2 enters the CNS via three main routes: the olfactory pathway (through the nose), trigeminal ganglia, and retrograde axonal transport. This neuroinvasion leads to neuroinflammation (characterized by activated microglia and astrocytes releasing inflammatory cytokines) and oxidative stress (with increased reactive oxygen species and cell apoptosis). (B) Medical gases intervention: Different medical gases exert neuroprotective effects through specific molecular mechanisms. Hyperbaric oxygen (O2) upregulates oxygen- and pressure-sensitive genes and promotes stem cell proliferation and neurogenesis, leading to enhanced neuroplasticity and improved cognitive function. Hydrogen (H) upregulates regulatory T cells (T-reg) and inhibits IL-1β and ROS production, reducing neuroinflammation. Xenon (Xe) inhibits NMDA receptors at the glycine site, reducing excitotoxicity and preserving neuronal function. Argon (Ar) modulates TLR2/4, activates the ERK1/2 pathway, and upregulates Nrf2, resulting in reduced oxidative stress and inhibition of apoptosis. Volatile anesthetics (isoflurane/sevoflurane/desflurane) inhibit the TLR-4/NF-κB pathway and activate HIF-1α, attenuating inflammatory responses and reducing pro-inflammatory cytokines. Collectively, these interventions contribute to improved neurological outcomes in long-COVID patients experiencing brain fog. Created with BioRender.com. CNS: Central nervous system; COVID-19: coronavirus disease 19; ERK1/2: extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1/2; HIF-1α: hypoxia-inducible factor 1-alpha; IL: interleukin; NF: nuclear factor; NMDA: N-methyl-D-aspartate; Nrf2: nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2; ROS: reactive oxygen species; SARS-CoV-2: severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2; TLR: Toll-like receptor
